key_insight: The paper shows how finite-time Lyapunov bounds for an associated SDE can be transferred into convergence-rate guarantees for stochastic gradient algorithms.
engineering_relevance: This gives practitioners a calculus-based route to prove and compare SGD convergence rates for existing and new optimization methods without doing a full stochastic analysis from scratch.
method: Construct an SDE that approximates the stochastic gradient algorithm.
Prove a finite-time Lyapunov generator inequality for the SDE.
Transfer the SDE rate bound back to the discrete algorithm under moment and smoothness conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical verification of finite-time convergence bounds and recovery of established rates for classical stochastic gradient methods.
watch_item: The approach depends on finding a suitable associated SDE and verifying moment/smoothness assumptions, which may be nontrivial for complex or nonstandard algorithms.
paper_title: A Rate Transfer Method: Convergence Rates in Stochastic Gradient Descent via Stochastic Calculus
